title: Geometric components of an affine scheme descend to a finite constant extension
statement:
Fix a prime power $q$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-pc-base-change]. There exist an integer $e\geq1$ and a finite set $I$ such that, with $k_e=\mathbf F_{q^e}\subset k$, there is a decomposition into nonempty open and closed affine subschemes
$$X_0\times_{k_0}k_e=\coprod_{i\in I}X_{i,e}.$$
Each $X_{i,e}$ is geometrically connected over $k_e$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and their base changes to $k$ are exactly the connected components of $X$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. If $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is smooth of relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], each $X_{i,e}\to\operatorname{Spec}k_e$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$. The empty scheme is allowed, with $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 038E, lemma-galois-action-connected-components-continuous, statement and proof (components descend to finite subextensions); Tag 0387, lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected; morphisms.tex Tags 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d)

proof.text: For every intermediate field $k_0\subseteq K\subseteq k$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $X_{0,K}$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{k_0}K)$. By clause (2) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], its structure morphism is of finite type. Thus [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra] makes $B\otimes_{k_0}K$ a finitely generated $K$-algebra. Applying [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] gives the descending-chain condition on closed subsets of $X_{0,K}$. In particular $X=X_{0,k}$ is a Noetherian topological space.

source.place: Tag 038E, final paragraph of proof: finite type base change and Noetherianity; schemes.tex Tag 01I4; morphisms.tex Tag 01T4

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open], $X$ has a finite set $I$ of nonempty connected components $U_i$, each open. They partition $X$: for any point $x$, the union of all connected subsets containing $x$ is connected, since in a separation every such subset must lie in the side containing $x$; this union is maximal. The same argument shows that two intersecting maximal connected subsets coincide. This uses the meaning of connectedness in [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Each $U_i$ is closed because its complement is the union of the other open components. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] every $U_i$ is quasi-compact. Regard $U_i$ as the open subscheme with the restricted structure sheaf.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-qc-open-fg-subalgebra] with base field $k_0$, scheme $X_0$, algebra $A=k$, and quasi-compact open $U_i\subset X$. For every $i\in I$ it gives a finitely generated $k_0$-subalgebra $A_i\subset k$ and a quasi-compact open $W_i\subset X_{0,A_i}$ such that $U_i$ is the inverse image of $W_i$ along $X\to X_{0,A_i}$. Only the openness and inverse-image equality are asserted at this point; clopenness and geometric connectedness downstairs will be proved below.

source.place: Tag 038E, proof of (b), using Tag 0388 (lemma-descend-open), statement and proof

proof.text: Choose a finite algebra generating set $S_i$ for each $A_i$ and put $S=\bigcup_{i\in I}S_i$, which is finite. Every element of $S$ is algebraic over $k_0$ because $k$ is an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension], the intermediate subfield $L=k_0(S)\subset k$ is finite-dimensional over $k_0$ and contains every $A_i$. Set $e=[L:k_0]\geq1$. A basis gives a bijection of sets $L\simeq k_0^{\{1,\ldots,e\}}$, so $|L|=q^e$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure] therefore gives $L=k_e=\mathbf F_{q^e}\subset k$. If $I$ is empty, take $S=\varnothing$ and $L=k_0$, so $e=1$.

source.place: Tag 09GH (lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated); finite-field naming as in the blueprint ancestor proof, second paragraph

proof.text: Write $Y=X_{0,L}$ and $p:X\to Y$. Pull the open immersion $W_i\hookrightarrow X_{0,A_i}$ back along $Y\to X_{0,A_i}$, obtaining an open subscheme $V_i\subset Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Its underlying open is the inverse image of $W_i$. The composite $X\to Y\to X_{0,A_i}$ is the canonical map induced by $A_i\subset L\subset k$. Hence $p^{-1}(V_i)=U_i$. The iterated-base-change identification in [def-pc-base-change] identifies $V_i\times_L k$ with the open subscheme $U_i$ of $X$, with its restricted structure sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0388, inverse-image description of descended opens; schemes.tex Tags 01JX, 01JY

proof.text: The map $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective]. Since $Y$ is affine by step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-surjective-base-change] imply that its base change $p:X\to Y$ is surjective. Thus the opens $V_i$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $Y$: the inverse image of $V_i\cap V_j$ is $U_i\cap U_j=\varnothing$ for $i\ne j$, and the inverse image of $Y\setminus\bigcup_i V_i$ is empty. A nonempty subset of $Y$ cannot have empty inverse image under a surjection. Moreover $V_i$ is nonempty because its inverse image is the nonempty $U_i$. The complement of $V_i$ is $\bigcup_{j\ne i}V_j$, so $V_i$ is also closed.

source.place: Tag 00FI (lemma-surjective-spec-radical-ideal), final base-change assertion; varieties.tex Tag 038E, assembly of descended components

proof.text: Let $R=B\otimes_{k_0}L$, so $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$. For each clopen $V_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] supplies an idempotent $a_i\in R$ with $V_i=D(a_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], this basic open is affine, with coordinate ring $R_{a_i}$. Put $X_{i,e}=V_i$ with its open-subscheme structure. The disjoint open cover of step 6 identifies $Y$ with $\coprod_{i\in I}X_{i,e}$ as schemes: the inclusions glue, and their inverses on each member of the cover glue to the inverse morphism. Thus this is a decomposition into nonempty open and closed affine subschemes.

source.place: Tag 00EE, clopen-idempotent correspondence; schemes.tex Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine); blueprint ancestor proof, second paragraph

proof.text: By step 5, $X_{i,e}\times_{k_e}k=U_i$, which is connected. The field $k$ is algebraically closed; it is also algebraic over $k_e$, since the nonzero polynomials over $k_0$ witnessing algebraicity remain nonzero over the subfield $k_e\subset k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Apply [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] over $k_e$ to conclude that $X_{i,e}$ is geometrically connected. Their base changes are exactly the components indexed by $I$. If $X_0$ is empty then $X$ and $Y$ are empty, $I=\varnothing$ and step 4 gives $e=1$; every assertion about an individual component is vacuous.

Finally suppose $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$. Clause (1) of [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] makes $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k_e$ smooth of relative dimension $d$. The inclusion $X_{i,e}\hookrightarrow Y$ is an open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] it is smooth of relative dimension zero. Clause (2) of the same permanence lemma makes the composite $X_{i,e}\to\operatorname{Spec}k_e$ smooth of relative dimension $0+d=d$, as required.
